name: Cozy House Hostel
detail: A small house located about a 10-minute walk from the train station. The room is small but suitable for a solo traveler to stay. There are shared bathrooms on each floor with good hot water pressure. Cleanliness is good, and most cooking utensils and dishes are provided. Above all, the staff is friendly.

name: Hualien Wow Hostel
detail: This is a review from a Japanese person. It was about 3,500 yen for a single room instead of a dormitory. The location is perfect, right in front of Hualien Station, with taxi stands, convenience stores, and breakfast spots nearby - absolutely perfect. The staff, while not fluent in Japanese, were kind and courteous. The atmosphere inside the hotel is lively, filled with backpackers. There is also a wealth of information on local tourist attractions posted on the bulletin board, showing the hotel's enthusiasm. The room was sufficiently spacious, and the shower has proper dividers so that the toilet doesn't get wet. If you're coming to Hualien, this place seems like the best choice, doesn't it? ^_^ It was a nice accommodation.

name: HUALIEN TOONG MAO RESORT
detail: It is somewhat distant from Hualien Station, and I think it would be difficult to access without a car. There is nothing around, but it has a resort hotel feel. There is both a bathtub and a shower. The room is spacious with twin beds. If you finish your meals and stay, you can relax. It takes about 15 minutes by car to get to the city center.

name: Sleeping Boot Hostel
detail: Host Yoshiei is fluent in English and very kind, providing detailed information about the night market via LINE. It's within walking distance from the station and bus terminal, the facilities are sufficient, and it was clean. The price is reasonable and I am satisfied.

name: Charming City Hotel Hualien
detail: The long-established chain hotel provides five-star level excellent service, with warm and comfortable soft sofas, a quiet and convenient spacious and bright decor. The overall design of the Hualien marble lobby is refreshing, and the rooms are clean and neat with double sinks and a separated wet and dry area. The housekeeping staff is very professional and attentive to cleaning and organizing. Whether at the front desk, housekeeping, or restaurant, all the staff members have a very friendly attitude. I highly recommend the long-established Xiangcheng Hotel.

name: Mini Voyage Hostel
detail: Advantages 1) Excellent location just a 5-minute walk from Hwa-Ryeon Station 2) Friendly staff who are fluent in English 3) Luggage can be stored at the front desk 4) Decent soundproofing, cozy lighting inside the accommodation, and overall cleanliness of the room 5) Good water pressure in the bathroom and cleanliness Disadvantages 1) No elevator, so luggage must be carried directly to higher floors 2) No other disadvantages come to mind

name: Kindness Hotel Hualien
detail: As per the prior reviews, everything was at the highest level despite being cheap. The room was very spacious, the cleaning was perfect, and it was rare in Taiwan to have a toilet equipped with a bidet. All meals and snacks in between were free, with a wide variety and everything was delicious. Laundry machines and bicycles were also free. The staff were all kind and full of a service spirit. From the station, it takes about 7 minutes to walk slowly in the rain with heavy luggage. There is nothing around the station, so the location of this hotel is just right. One disappointing thing was that they do not handle currency exchange. In Hualien, cash payments are common, and I had problems because I didn't have cash and couldn't exchange money.

name: Xiang Pin Hotel
detail: The room is very spacious. The facilities are decent for the price. There is a thick mattress bed placed on the flooring, and I stayed for three nights, but there was no bed making. There is no elevator, and the room is on the third floor. The old-fashioned building has window blackout blinds that give a retro feel reminiscent of an 18th-century Asian street corner, which I liked, and the room was clean. However, during check-in, there was no one present, so I had to become friends on LINE using a QR code at the entrance and communicate with the host through LINE, which may be a bit challenging for those who cannot use English or Chinese. However, there is a night market within a 10-minute walk and the Chongqing Market, which opens early in the morning, so I had no trouble finding food. It's only a 15-minute bus ride from Hualien Train Station, getting off at Zhonghua Road and walking 5 minutes, or getting off at Dongdaemun Night Market and walking 5 minutes, making it very convenient. It is a must-see for those who prioritize the price of accommodation.

name: Finders Hotel Hualien Wen Hua
detail: The location is great, close to the night market, Chongqing morning market, and coastal park. The facilities were all clean. There is no laundry service, but there is a coin laundry conveniently located right in front of the hotel. The lobby has plenty of chairs and sofas, and there are free drinks and snacks available. There are no YouBikes in Hualien, but the hotel offers free bike rentals that even come with helmets. All the staff were kind and friendly. This time, I probably had the smallest room, but it was clean despite being small. I want to give it a perfect score, but one disappointing thing was that there was no refrigerator in the room. This might be because it was a budget room, so I recommend confirming this when making a reservation. There is a convenience store just a 1-2 minute walk away. There are no Uber taxis in Hualien, but the staff readily helped arrange a taxi when asked. I would definitely like to use this hotel again for my next trip to Hualien.

name: Kadda Hotel
detail: The staff at the front desk are really kind. They readily lend their umbrellas on rainy days, and even though communication is difficult due to my being Korean, they genuinely try to help and greet you with a smile throughout. I especially appreciated the tall, handsome male staff member, the man with glasses, and the female staff member with glasses, who treated us warmly every time we passed by and showed true kindness even as we checked out. There is a restaurant nearby that serves delicious squid chicken soup, and I visited Chilsungdam Beach and a Chongyobing shop, which were about 40-50 minutes away by the bike they lent us. The buses didn’t come often, but I confirmed real-time locations on the Ibus site, which helped us save on taxi fare when heading to the train station. There were quite a few bikes available, and they also rent out electric bikes for a fee. The pool was long and big, which was great, and the breakfast seemed Taiwanese but suited my taste well. The salted boiled duck eggs in rice porridge were delicious, and I had two bowls. The dim sum was also tasty. Overall, it was a great hotel, and I recommend it. (When heading to the Chongyobing store, take the main road. I was scared when I went into the inner Taiwan construction area because of the stray dogs.)
